method_card.title: Electrical Power and Energy Bills
method_card.content:
Two families of question live here: electrical power and energy bills.

Power: use P = VI when you know voltage and current, P = IÂ²R when you know current and resistance, and E = QV for the energy a charge carries. Square the current before multiplying in P = IÂ²R.

Bills: unit slips cost the most marks. Put power in kilowatts and time in hours, then energy (kWh) = power Ã— time and cost = energy Ã— price per kWh. There are 1,000 W in a kilowatt and 100 pence in a pound.

gold.hint: Use Vp Ã— Ip = Vs Ã— Is and rearrange for the secondary current.
gold.display: A step-up transformer increases voltage from 25,000 V to 400,000 V. The primary current is 800 A. Calculate the secondary current in amperes.

guided_steps.say: A transformer conserves power: Vp Ã— Ip = Vs Ã— Is. Rearrange for the secondary current: Is = (Vp Ã— Ip) Ã· Vs. Check whether your board gives you this equation.

guided_steps.pre: Divide by the secondary voltage: 20,000,000 Ã· 400,000 =

guided_steps.done: 20,000,000 W in and out, so Is = 50 A.

misconceptions.message: Vp Ã— Ip = Vs Ã— Is, so Is = (Vp Ã— Ip) Ã· Vs = (25,000 Ã— 800) Ã· 400,000 = 50 A. Dividing by the wrong voltage gives 12,800 A.

misconceptions.message: Square the current first: 100Â² = 10,000, then Ã— 2 = 20,000 W. Using 100 Ã— 2 = 200 forgets the square.

bronze.hint: Multiply the voltage by the current.

misconceptions.message: Multiply, do not divide: P = V Ã— I = 230 Ã— 4 = 920 W.

misconceptions.message: Energy is power times time: E = 2 Ã— 0.5 = 1 kWh, not power divided by time.

bronze.hint: Multiply the number of units by the price of one unit.

guided_steps.say: Cost = energy (kWh) Ã— price per kWh. The energy is 5 kWh and each kWh costs 30p.

guided_steps.pre: Warm up: 2 kWh would cost 2 Ã— 30 =

guided_steps.done: Â£1.50 for 5 units, so 150p is right.
guided_steps.hint: A hundred pence in a pound.

bronze.equation_hint: Cost = energy (kWh) Ã— price per kWh

misconceptions.message: Cost = energy Ã— price = 5 Ã— 30 = 150p. Do not divide.

bronze.hint: Square the current, then multiply by the resistance.
bronze.display: A resistor has resistance 20 Î© and carries a current of 2 A. Calculate the power dissipated.

guided_steps.say: For a resistor, P = IÂ²R. Square the current before you multiply.

guided_steps.done: 4 is 2Â², so I = 2 A. P = 80 W.

misconceptions.message: Square the current first: P = IÂ²R = 2Â² Ã— 20 = 4 Ã— 20 = 80 W. Using 2 Ã— 20 = 40 forgets the square.

guided_steps.say: Energy carried by a charge: E = Q Ã— V. Q is 200 C and V is 6 V.
